bigpic.b: Nvidia froze AI server shipments to Southeast Asia
bigpic.t: telling partners to halt deliveries to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia after a US rule targeting Chinese access to rented computing.

bigpic.b: Europe rallied on softer US tariff plans
bigpic.t: with the Stoxx 600 up 1.7% after Washington said new duties would be capped at rates agreed in trade deals.

bigpic.b: Brent climbed toward $96 on new Gulf attacks
bigpic.t: while budget carrier Norse Atlantic grounded every flight amid high fuel costs and warned it may file for bankruptcy.

stories.h: European stocks jump 1.7% as Washington signals lower caps on new tariffs
stories.sum: The Stoxx 600 rose 1.7% to 636.44 by 10:20 GMT on Thursday, led by gains of about 2.5% in tech and 2.4% in banks. The US Trade Representative's office said on Wednesday it intends to cap new tariffs at the lower rates set in trade deals, such as the 15% agreed with the EU last year.
stories.why: Capped duties limit the worst-case hit to European exporters and reduce uncertainty for companies planning their 2027 trade with the US.

stories.h: Kospi gives up most of its rebound as retail investors sell; Nikkei ends 0.84% up
stories.sum: Korea's Kospi closed up 0.29% at 4,711.21 after rising more than 1% in the morning, as individual investors sold a net 1.04 trillion won and foreigners 112 billion won. Japan's Nikkei 225 finished 0.84% higher. Wall Street is closed for Thanksgiving and trades a shortened session on Friday.
stories.why: Retail selling into the bounce shows local investors remain wary after Wednesday's 6% plunge in the Kospi.

stories.h: US PCE inflation hits 3.8% in October as third-quarter growth is revised up to 4.3%
stories.sum: The Fed's preferred price gauge rose 0.3% on the month and 3.8% from a year earlier, while core prices climbed 3.3%, a tenth above forecasts. Third-quarter GDP growth was revised to an annualised 4.3% from 3.4%. Consumer spending was flat after inflation and the saving rate stood at 4.1%.
stories.why: Hot prices alongside strong growth make a Fed hike on 9 December near certain, pushing borrowing costs higher across the economy.

stories.h: Nvidia halts AI server shipments to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia
stories.sum: Nvidia has told manufacturing partners to stop delivering servers to the four countries, the Financial Times reported, with Dell and Supermicro telling customers the shipments are not authorised. It follows a US Commerce rule closing a cloud-rental loophole, which gives providers 90 days to get licences. Nvidia booked $104B of revenue through its Singapore unit in 2025.
stories.why: Southeast Asia's data-centre boom, including RM123.5B of Malaysian investment approved in nine months, depends on steady access to Nvidia hardware.

stories.h: Kioxia closes 12.6% higher and SoftBank 7.3% as Asian chip stocks recover
stories.sum: Memory maker Kioxia ended up 12.57% at 7,762 yen and SoftBank Group 7.32% higher at 2,894 yen in Tokyo, trimming a morning gain of nearly 10%. In Seoul, SK hynix closed 2.23% higher at 1,053,000 won, while Samsung Electronics rose just 0.35% to 171,300 won.
stories.why: Chip makers dominate Asia's markets, so their recovery decides whether doubts over AI spending turn into a broader regional sell-off.

stories.h: EU proposes a €50B tech equity fund and a Quantum Act favouring European suppliers
stories.sum: The European Commission on 25 Nov set €50B as the target size of a sovereign tech equity fund, alongside a draft Quantum Act that would reserve some public contracts for EU-controlled suppliers. Public quantum funding in 2025 was €8.6B in Europe against €13.6B in China, and EU quantum startups raised €1.1B privately versus €7B in the US.
stories.why: Buy-European rules could shut US and Asian vendors out of some contracts, though EU governments and Parliament must still approve the plan.

stories.h: Bank of Korea raises its rate to 3.25% and lifts 2027 growth forecast to 4.1%
stories.sum: The central bank raised its base rate by a quarter point to 3.25%, the highest since November 2024, in a 5-2 vote, its third increase this year. It lifted its growth forecasts to 3.9% for 2026 and 4.1% for 2027 on booming chip exports, with inflation at 2.8% in October against a 2% target.
stories.why: Hiking during a stock rout shows the central bank putting inflation and a heated housing market ahead of market stress.

stories.h: EU leaders take up ECB succession at Brussels summit; Hernández de Cos is favourite
stories.sum: ECB leadership appointments are on the agenda of the 26-27 Nov special summit, alongside the 2028-2034 budget and Ukraine's 2027 funding, and summit chair António Costa wants such posts settled well in advance. Pablo Hernández de Cos is widely expected to get the presidency, with Spain's backing and reportedly that of Macron and Merz.
stories.why: The next president will steer euro-area interest rates for eight years, shaping lending margins and bond yields across Europe.

stories.h: FSB keeps 29 banks on its global systemic list, moving BNP Paribas up a bucket
stories.sum: The Financial Stability Board's 2026 list, published 25 Nov using end-2025 data, names the same 29 banks as last year. BNP Paribas moves to bucket 3 from bucket 2, raising its required capital buffer, while MUFG drops to bucket 1. The new requirements take effect from 1 January 2028.
stories.why: Bucket changes alter how much extra capital the largest lenders must hold, shaping their room for lending, buybacks and dividends.

stories.h: Bitcoin holds above $60,000 as large holders sell and ETF outflows set a record
stories.sum: Bitcoin traded near $60,460 at 8am Singapore time, up about 1% in 24 hours after dipping to about $57,500 on Wednesday. US spot bitcoin ETFs have lost about $4.94B in November, their worst month since launching in January 2024. Santiment says wallets holding 10 to 10,000 BTC have shed about 150,000 BTC since 2 Nov.
stories.why: Steady selling by funds and big holders has removed key buyers, leaving prices exposed to swings in leveraged trading.

stories.h: Bitcoin reserve bill heads to the House floor with little time left this session
stories.sum: The House Financial Services Committee on 24 Nov sent Rep. Nick Begich's American Reserve Modernization Act to the full House. It would write a federal bitcoin reserve into law, built mainly from forfeited coins, and bar selling them for at least 20 years. Congress adjourns within weeks, and Polymarket puts a reserve by year-end at 4%.
stories.why: A legal ban on sales would lock up a large government holding, but if the bill stalls it must restart in the next Congress.

stories.h: US moves to seize funds from Binance's $6B hack, naming North Korea's Lazarus
stories.sum: A Justice Department forfeiture complaint filed in Washington on 23 Nov says hackers took about $6B in crypto from Binance around 29 Oct. It targets assets frozen under a 12 Nov court order served on USDC issuer Circle, and blames North Korea's Lazarus Group, whose members posed as job recruiters.
stories.why: Freezing stolen stablecoins through issuers like Circle shows how regulated tokens give authorities a recovery tool that bitcoin lacks.

stories.h: Sanofi agrees to buy Insmed for $41B in pharma's biggest deal since 2023
stories.sum: Sanofi will pay $175 a share, a 46% premium to Insmed's 18 Nov price, gaining Brinsupri for bronchiectasis, with $1.09B of sales in the first nine months, plus Arikayce and the Phase 3 lung drug TPIP. Closing is expected in the first half of 2027. Sanofi shares rose 9.8% on 24 Nov and 4.9% on 25 Nov after upgrades.
stories.why: Gives Sanofi new respiratory growth before Dupixent, about 40% of group revenue, loses its main US patent in 2031.

stories.h: EU Parliament approves pharma law overhaul and Critical Medicines Act
stories.sum: Parliament gave final approval on 25 Nov to the EU pharmaceutical reform agreed in December 2025, which sets eight years of data protection and caps total regulatory protection at 11 years. It also passed the Critical Medicines Act by 592 votes to 35, adding an EU preference in public tenders and support for European manufacturing.
stories.why: New exclusivity rules change the revenue runway for drugs sold in Europe and push supply chains for critical medicines back onto the continent.

stories.h: FDA approves Cogent's bezuclastinib combination for advanced GIST
stories.sum: The FDA cleared Cogent Biosciences' Ekitna (bezuclastinib) with Pfizer's older drug sunitinib for adults with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumours previously treated with imatinib. In the Phase 3 PEAK trial, the combination held off disease progression for a median 16.5 months, against 9.2 months on sunitinib alone.
stories.why: Adds a new later-line option in a rare cancer and lifts the commercial prospects of a mid-sized oncology biotech.

stories.h: Brent nears $96 as more ships are hit near Dubai and Saudi Arabia downs drones
stories.sum: Brent gained 1.5% to $96.03 a barrel on Thursday after a 3.5% jump on Wednesday. UKMTO said a projectile exploded near a tanker about 93km west of Dubai, and three more eastbound ships were reported hit. Saudi Arabia said it destroyed four drones aimed at its Ras Tanura refinery, which Yemen's Houthis said they targeted.
stories.why: Repeated attacks around the Gulf's main export routes keep a risk premium in crude despite rising stockpiles and a forecast surplus.

stories.h: Boehly's Eldridge leads a US-backed deal for Lukoil's international assets
stories.sum: A consortium led by Todd Boehly's Eldridge, including the US International Development Finance Corporation, UAE-based Catena Investment Holding and Xtellus Partners, agreed on 25 Nov to take over Lukoil's foreign business. It spans oil and gas assets in Bulgaria, Romania, Africa and the Middle East plus fuel stations abroad. No price was given; US Treasury approval is still required.
stories.why: The deal would move refineries and oilfields out of sanctioned Russian ownership, with Washington taking a stake through the DFC.

stories.h: OPEC+ meets Sunday on 2027 quotas as Iraq disputes its capacity estimate
stories.sum: Ministers meet on 29 Nov to set 2027 output using the group's first capacity review. Iraq, given a preliminary capacity of 4.9M barrels a day, wants a higher figure and has warned it could leave if its quota is not raised, and Kazakhstan is also pushing back. Russia's Alexander Novak says the review should finish by year-end.
stories.why: The quota split decides which producers can pump more in 2027 as the market tips toward surplus.

stories.h: EU caps Chinese-built hybrid imports at 191,780 cars until June
stories.sum: The EU adopted provisional quotas on 24 Nov limiting hybrid imports from China and other countries from 1 Dec to 18 Jun 2027. China-built plug-in, full and mild hybrids share a cap of 191,780 cars across three periods, while range-extended EVs and EU-built hybrids fall outside it. China's commerce ministry reserved the right to challenge the move at the WTO.
stories.why: Hybrids escaped the EU's extra duties on Chinese electric cars, so quotas narrow a key path into Europe for Chinese brands.

stories.h: China's car sales slump 27% in October, setting off a wave of discounts
stories.sum: Passenger car retail sales fell 27.1% from a year earlier to 1.643M in October, and new-energy vehicle sales dropped 13.7% to 1.109M, Gasgoo data show. Sales in the first half of November were down 25%. At least 10 carmakers have signalled price cuts, and Tesla on 24 Nov extended cheaper Model 3 financing to 31 Dec.
stories.why: A sharp demand slump deepens China's price war, squeezing margins for local brands and foreign rivals alike.

stories.h: EU delays its vote on Tesla's Full Self-Driving system to 15 December
stories.sum: The EU's Technical Committee for Motor Vehicles will meet on 15 Dec instead of 1 Dec to consider Tesla's supervised FSD, a European Commission spokesperson told Reuters. Approval needs 15 of 27 member states representing 65% of the EU population; France and Sweden have raised concerns about speeding. Tesla shares were down about 5% in Wednesday trading.
stories.why: Europe is a key test of Tesla's bet that driving software, not just car sales, will justify its valuation.

stories.h: Poundland falls into administration, putting about 11,000 jobs at risk
stories.sum: The UK discount chain appointed AlixPartners as administrators on 25 Nov after sale talks with bidders including Martin Property Group failed to find a solvent deal. Its roughly 600 stores keep trading while buyers are sought, and Tesco and B&M are reported to be interested in parts. Owner Gordon Brothers bought Poundland for £1 last year.
stories.why: A break-up would let rivals such as Tesco and B&M pick up sites, reshaping Britain's discount high street before Christmas.

stories.h: Abercrombie & Fitch raises its outlook after an 11% sales jump; shares surge
stories.sum: Net sales rose 11% to $1.44B in the quarter to 31 Oct and comparable sales grew 6%, while diluted earnings reached $3.82 a share against $2.36 a year earlier. The retailer now expects full-year sales growth of about 6% and earnings of $13.70 to $13.90 a share. Its shares were up 22.5% on Tuesday morning.
stories.why: A raised forecast heading into the holidays shows demand holding up for some apparel brands despite high inflation.

stories.h: US online holiday spending tops $82.5B so far, up 9.1%, Adobe says
stories.sum: Shoppers spent more than $82.5B online from 1 to 22 Nov, and buy now, pay later spending rose 6.5% to $6.1B, Adobe Analytics data show. Adobe expects $6.9B on Thanksgiving, $12.9B on Black Friday and $15.1B on Cyber Monday. Visits to retail sites referred by AI assistants are up 127%.
stories.why: Solid online demand into the holiday peak supports retailers' fourth-quarter forecasts despite inflation running near 4%.

stories.h: Disney's Hexed opens with about $7.8M on Wednesday as its holiday forecast slips
stories.sum: Hexed took an estimated $7.8M on its opening day in 3,725 theatres, including $2.1M from Tuesday previews, and its five-day forecast was cut to $35M to $40M from $40M to $45M. Universal's Focker In-Law is tracking about $36M, while Lionsgate's Sunrise on the Reaping is on pace for $85M or more over the five days.
stories.why: A soft start for Hexed, which cost more than $200M, adds pressure on Disney's original animated films.

stories.h: Unilever halves UK TV ad spending and cuts its Channel 4 budget by about 92%
stories.sum: Unilever has cut its UK TV advertising by just over half this year compared with 2025, The Guardian reported, after spending about £92M in 2025. Its spending with Channel 4 fell about 92%, Sky's sales arm 44% and ITV 42%, as the consumer group shifts money to a creator network of more than 500,000 people.
stories.why: One of Britain's biggest advertisers moving to influencers deepens the squeeze on broadcasters, with Channel 4 already cutting 340 jobs.

stories.h: Norse Atlantic grounds all flights and says it will seek bankruptcy without new funds
stories.sum: The Norwegian long-haul carrier suspended all operations on 26 Nov, a day after a funding warning sent its shares down 85%. The board is weighing a takeover by an outside party and talks with holders of a $52M secured bond, and plans to file for bankruptcy without urgent short-term financing. Seven routes and two planned Thai services are cancelled.
stories.why: Its collapse would remove a low-cost transatlantic rival and shows how high fuel costs are straining thinly financed long-haul airlines.

stories.h: US proposes a 10% tariff on Brazilian aircraft, ending Embraer's exemption
stories.sum: USTR proposed on 25 Nov a 10% duty on finished aircraft from Brazil, including planes and helicopters, ending an exemption granted in July when a 25% tariff hit other Brazilian goods. Comments run from 27 Nov to 30 Dec, with a hearing on 14 Jan. Embraer, which supplies E175 regional jets to US carriers, fell as much as 9.2%.
stories.why: A duty would raise costs for US regional airlines flying Embraer jets and break with the industry's tradition of tariff-free aircraft trade.

stories.h: Airbus agrees to sell its US space systems unit to Cerberus to focus on aviation
stories.sum: Cerberus Capital Management will buy the space systems business of Airbus U.S. Space & Defense, based at a roughly 200,000 sq ft site in Merritt Island, Florida, near Kennedy Space Center. No price was disclosed and the deal is expected to close by year-end. Airbus U.S. said it will focus on core aviation and expand its autonomous aircraft work.
stories.why: The exit narrows Airbus's US defence business to aviation, betting on autonomous military aircraft rather than satellites.

stories.h: Vanke seeks a three-year delay on a 1.2B yuan bond as its dollar debt slides
stories.sum: China Vanke wants to push back repayment of 1.2B yuan of principal due 15 Dec by three years while paying the 3% coupon on time, and has floated upfront payments of less than half the 40% it paid in earlier deals. Its 2029 dollar bond fell 3.5 cents to 43.3 cents. Contracted sales are down 48.3% from a year earlier.
stories.why: Repeated extensions at a developer backed by state-owned Shenzhen Metro keep doubts alive over how far Beijing will go to prevent defaults.

stories.h: US new home sales jump 14.2% in October despite 7% mortgage rates
stories.sum: Sales of new single-family homes rose to an annual rate of 701,000 in October from a downwardly revised 614,000 in September, Census data show, and were 7.5% higher than a year earlier. Supply fell to eight months, the lowest this year. Year-to-date sales remain 3% behind 2025, the National Association of Home Builders says.
stories.why: A surprise rebound offers builders some relief, though high rates keep resale activity near decade lows.

stories.h: Hong Kong home prices slip 0.6% in October while rents hit another record
stories.sum: The official private home price index fell 0.59% to 319 in October, ending two months of gains, though prices are still up 6.48% this year and 8.17% from a year earlier. The rental index rose 0.47% to a record 213.2, its 12th straight monthly rise, Rating and Valuation Department data released on 26 Nov show.
stories.why: Softer prices alongside record rents suggest buyers are hesitating while landlords keep benefiting from strong tenant demand.

stories.h: Singapore factory output rises 6.1% in October as precision engineering jumps 54%
stories.sum: Manufacturing output grew 6.1% from a year earlier, up from 5.0% in September, and rose 7.1% on the month after seasonal adjustment, EDB data show. Excluding volatile biomedical output, it climbed 12.1%. Precision engineering surged 54.1% and electronics 6.6%, while biomedical fell 35.8% and transport engineering 5.3%.
stories.why: AI-driven demand for chipmaking equipment and electronics is carrying Singapore's growth as it faces new US tariff threats.

stories.h: US proposes tariffs of up to 20% on Singapore and 18% on Malaysia
stories.sum: USTR proposed duties on all goods from 14 economies on 25 Nov, ranging from 15% for the EU and Japan to 35% for Vietnam. Singapore's rate could drop to 10% with a trade deal, while Malaysia's could rise to 25% if talks fail. Chips and palm oil are exempt. Comments are due 5 Jan and hearings start 25 Jan.
stories.why: Singapore would face a higher rate than Japan or Korea, raising costs for exporters outside the chip exemption from early 2027.

stories.h: Malaysia wants priority over other lenders if it steps in to support AirAsia
stories.sum: Second Finance Minister Amir Hamzah Azizan told parliament on 26 Nov that public funds must rank ahead of other creditors if the government backs the airline, though no support has been agreed. AirAsia aims to raise up to $1B in international debt plus RM700M in local credit lines between December and February. Its shares have lost about 72% this year.
stories.why: AirAsia holds about 60% of Malaysia's domestic air market, so its funding affects fares, connectivity and tourism.

stories.h: KLCI ends 0.55% higher but gives back much of its morning rally
stories.sum: The FBM KLCI closed at 1,570.98, up 8.69 points or 0.55%, after reaching about 1,579 by late morning. Turnover rose to 3.35 billion shares worth RM3.29B, though losers outnumbered gainers 703 to 412. The ringgit opened firmer at 4.1135 to the US dollar from 4.1170.
stories.why: Gains were concentrated in blue chips while most shares fell, a sign local investors remain cautious despite the regional rebound.
